content:
Plan for Phase 45: Cockpit lanes — Lead | Reviewer, each in its own pane (3.8). Plan at docs/phases/cockpit-lanes.md (branch phase-45-cockpit-lanes @ fd8b204); roadmap entry added; Phase 44 (saloon) moves to 3.9 and now depends on 45.

Problem (arbiter walk-through 2026-08-17, later — docs/cockpit-issues.md): the shared newest-first Activity log puts the reviewer's running review above the lead's chat you were typing in, interleaved with pre-checks/starts; Lead and Reviewer are not clearly labeled; the loop starts with the lead so the reviewer "up above" is unexpected; seeing the reviewer means scrolling away.

Design (ux-design-guide; arbiter confirmed the two-pane structure): two lanes side by side in loop order — `<lead> — lead` | token | `<reviewer> — reviewer` — each a timeline in time order, newest at the foot. Lead lane = today's chat (messages, picker, composer at the foot) merged in time with the lead's cycle-turn cards (streaming when running). Reviewer lane = per round: pre-check → review (streams in place) → verdict word from /api/rounds (approved / changes requested / escalated / question for you), review lenses for panels. Working lane pulses; nothing to scroll to. Tabs: Rounds · Diff · Usage · Notes; the flat activity list stays as an "all activity" disclosure on Rounds. Needs-you keeps the arbiter's things (briefs, starts, lost turns).

Scope: B markup (lanes replace #cycle + the Lead tab; ids listed), C JS (renderLanes, upsertReviewerCard, renderLeadTimeline keyed/patched — no container wipe; auto-scroll at the foot; gate line; stream registry reused), D CSS (grid, stack < 1000px lead first), E docs + two screenshots recaptured, F tests (source guards incl. text-nodes-only in the lane block and the Phase 37 XSS guard kept; verdict map exactly six actions; behavioural node tests: reviewer ascending + patched-in-place with verdict, lead merge in time order without wipe, role split). Read model: no server change required; optional additive `activity_payload(role=)` filter if the merge needs it. Success criteria: reviewer visible without scrolling; labels/order; one home per agent; nothing rebuilt; suite green via the gate.

The lane model and scope boundary are strong. Please resolve these implementation-contract gaps in the plan before approval:

1. The compatibility rule says `#tab-lead-name` stays, but Scope B removes `#tab-lead` and only defines `#lane-lead-name`. Today `renderNow()` unconditionally writes `$('tab-lead-name').textContent`; removing the tab without moving/updating that write causes a null-element error. Specify the replacement (for example, retarget to `#lane-lead-name`) and update the compatibility statement/tests accordingly.

2. The all-activity markup shows only `#activity` inside `#all-activity`, while current `loadActivity()` unconditionally uses `#activity-empty`, `#activity-more`, and `#activity-meta`. Scope B also removes `#activity-head`, which currently owns the latter. Either retain/move all three supporting elements into the disclosure or explicitly refactor `loadActivity()` and its guards; include this in the markup and test plan.

3. With the Lead tab removed, the current refresh path only calls `loadLead(false)` when `activeTab() === 'lead'`. The lead lane is always visible, so scope C must explicitly change `refreshAll()` to keep conversation data/streams fresh on the normal page refresh (and describe the no-conversation empty state). Otherwise the lead timeline will be stale or empty outside the deleted tab.

Round 2 — addresses reviewer r1 (plan @ 45f... see branch phase-45-cockpit-lanes HEAD "docs(phase-45): plan round 2").

1. `#tab-lead-name`: the tab goes entirely (`#tab-lead`, `#tab-lead-name`, `#lead-dot`, `#panel-lead`, `#lead-title`); `renderNow` retargets the lead's-name write to `#lane-lead-name`; the compatibility rule now lists every id that moves or goes and states that no JS write to a removed id survives; a source guard iterates the removed ids and asserts no `$('<id>')` remains in cockpit.js.
2. All-activity: the disclosure markup now carries `#activity`, `#activity-empty`, `#activity-more` and `#activity-meta` (moved from the removed `#activity-head` into the summary) so `loadActivity()` is reused unchanged; the guard asserts all four ids sit inside `#all-activity`.
3. Refresh path: `refreshAll` calls `loadLead(false)` unconditionally (guarded), the `activeTab() === 'lead'` branches go, one `/api/activity` fetch feeds both lanes and the disclosure, `renderLeadTimeline()` is a keyed merge that runs after either `loadConversation` or `loadActivity` resolves (arrival order irrelevant); the no-conversation empty state (cards if any + "No messages yet…" at the foot; composer enabled when the lead validates, else disabled with the reason) is specified.

Approved. Round 2 resolves the removed-ID contract, retains all all-activity support elements, and makes lead conversation loading unconditional for the always-visible lead lane. The guards and behavioural coverage make the two-pane implementation actionable.
